A-AKI SUSHI

Is A-AKI SUSHI clean? Mostly — a B (85/100) at its latest inspection, June 12, 2026. Inspectors cited no violations.

No violations were itemized at that visit. That puts it safer than 30% of Orange County restaurants we grade. The trend has been improving. Diner rating: 4.1 from 1,491 reviews. Menus here flag vegetarian, dairy-free, keto, paleo, and other dietary options.

    I called the night before to confirm if we could use two Groupons (set of 4 and set of 2) for our birthday group, they confirmed we could. I bought the Groupon then called back to RSVP for the next night, I redeemed the Groupon codes for the staff which was requested from both Groupons. Next night, we ate, aftwards got the bill and saw only the 4 group Groupon was applied. Upon clarification, the manager told us it was only one Groupon per table and they cannot do anything about it.   • ★★★★★ June 17, 2026

    My family and I had an amazing experience at A-Aki Sushi & Steakhouse - Avalon. The food was fresh, flavorful, and beautifully prepared. The sushi rolls were excellent, the hibachi was cooked perfectly, and the portions were very generous. The staff was friendly, attentive, and made us feel welcome from the moment we walked in. The restaurant has a great atmosphere that’s perfect for both family dinners and special occasions. Everything arrived quickly, and the quality of the food exceeded our expectations. If you’re looking for great sushi, hibachi, and outstanding service in Avalon Park, this is definitely a place worth visiting.

  • ★★★☆☆ April 7, 2026

    I recently tried the BBQ at A-Aki Sushi & Steakhouse Avalon for the first time. I’ve been there before for sushi and have never had a bad experience-at most, service was a bit slow, but the food has always been enjoyable. Unfortunately, my BBQ experience wasn’t as great. It was just two of us dining, and the restaurant was empty when we arrived, yet service still took a while. It seemed like there wasn’t enough staff at first, and I even wondered if our server was the only one working in that area. As more customers started coming in later, our server became more active in the area, but the initial service felt limited. The BBQ price was $29.99 per person. The food itself wasn’t bad—the short ribs were pretty good. I didn’t catch my server’s name during the visit, but my receipt listed her as Sarah I. When we received our check, I noticed that a 20% gratuity had already been added for just two people. According to Sarah, this is automatic regardless of service and is “how it is everywhere.” That surprised me, as I’ve usually only seen automatic gratuity applied to larger groups (typically 6 or more, often around 18%). For comparison, I recently dined at Gen BBQ in Waterford with four people and did not have an automatic 20% gratuity added. I gave my server at Gen a 25% gratuity anyways cause she was amazing! Overall, the experience was okay, but the slow service and unexpected gratuity policy made it less enjoyable. I’m curious if this practice is actually common everywhere…

  • ★★☆☆☆ March 14, 2026

    I had the Korean BBQ. First thing I noticed was they laid parchment paper on the grill and said it needed to stay on. That really messed with the quality of the food because we couldn’t properly render the fat on the cuts of meat. It also would burn the paper and overall made the experience worse. The meat itself wasn’t the best quality; very tough and chewy. The marinades also weren’t good. Most lacking salt, the bulgogi was basically just brown sugar. The portions per food order were tiny. For example, if you order spring rolls, they bring out one spring roll cut in half. This wouldn’t be too bad if the meat and appetizers came out quickly, but you’ll wait about 15 minutes to get the meat out. It’s raw meat so I didn’t quite understand that. Maybe there was something going on in the kitchen. All that said, the servers were very nice, I don’t think it was their fault the food took forever to come out. Overall, this is without a doubt the worst KBB I’ve had in Orlando (I’ve been to 3 other restaurants).

  • ★★★★★ March 13, 2026

    A few weeks ago, I dined in for dinner at A-aki in Avalon Park with my family. As a regular patron, I continue to be impressed by the consistently high quality of both the food and the service. The newly introduced menu offers a wide variety of options. I would like to specifically acknowledge Amanda, whose attentive and cheerful service greatly enhanced our dining experience, even during peak hours. Despite the busy environment, she maintained a positive attitude and ensured we were well cared for. We look forward to returning to A-aki as usual.

  • ★★★☆☆ March 10, 2026

    I wanted to be able to leave a higher review but too many mistakes were made. Ordered the Tito's vodka and got regular. Ok no biggie. I got a roll for my main meal (we did the all you can eat even though we weren't even offered the option - I had to ask for it ) and my husband got fried rice and chicken katsu . After waiting another 20 min after I got my roll so we could eat our mains together, I asked our server if it was coming out soon and he brought the paper we ordered on . He pointed out we got all the appetizers and my roll; he didn't see the problem. I showed him they completely missed my husband's dinner. Ok fine it took a while but that came out. Then I ordered a plum wine from the Happy Hour menu. When we got the bill they charged us full price for the wine. I brought it up to the server and he stated sorry the system won't allow it. I said but it's on the happy hour menu. He said well it doesn't let me . He wound up discounting it after but as of server he should have informed us before just charging us. The food overall was good. No complaints. But the experience with the server left a bad taste.
